investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-eligible nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~149 seconds, the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining peer-pod VM slots, either because existing remote agent pods are consuming all slots or the node-level quota is set too low for the current workload.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to exactly those 2 nodes; if those 2 are also resource-exhausted, no fallback exists.

TERTIARY — peer-pod provider or kata-containers runtime capacity issue: the underlying VM provider backing kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., cloud VM quota, peer-pod daemon capacity) may have hit an external limit, causing the kubelet on those 2 nodes to report the resource as insufficient even if Kubernetes-level accounting appears available.

QUATERNARY — eval probe cleanup gap: if a prior eval run did not fully clean up remote agent pods (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), leaked pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, artificially exhausting capacity for subsequent runs.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that counts pods in a pending or stuck state requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm and fails if any are older than a configurable threshold, catching cleanup failures early.

Parameterize the remote-agent-create eval with a shorter scheduling timeout and a distinct 'Unschedulable' status code so the failure message can be machine-classified separately from other agent creation failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-20T17:01–17:06Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract violation for remote-agent-state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to provision a remote-agent pod times out unscheduled (~143–149 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state and runtime checks unreachable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-eligible nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~149 seconds, the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining peer-pod VM slots, either because existing remote agent pods are consuming all slots or the node-level quota is set too low for the current workload.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to exactly those 2 nodes; if those 2 are also resource-exhausted, no fallback exists.

TERTIARY — peer-pod provider or kata-containers runtime capacity issue: the underlying VM provider backing kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., cloud VM quota, peer-pod daemon capacity) may have hit an external limit, causing the kubelet on those 2 nodes to report the resource as insufficient even if Kubernetes-level accounting appears available.

QUATERNARY — eval probe cleanup gap: if a prior eval run did not fully clean up remote agent pods (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), leaked pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, artificially exhausting capacity for subsequent runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a total contract gap against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible regardless of preemption. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and no preemption victims available, every eval pod that attempts to create a remote agent is stuck Unschedulable until the eval timeout fires. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata peer-pod pool; it is an eval-detected signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident, because no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, latencyMs=149847, endedAt=2026-06-20T17:04:07.312Z
failed-check.evidence: empty object — zero evidence fields returned, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with createAgent never completing

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — if the pod is unschedulable this call blocks until timeout and no evidence is written

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the eval timed out at latencyMs=149492 well before the outage threshold, confirming the failure is scheduling-driven not a latency regression
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=149492 — the ~149s wall time matches the scheduler message '144s unscheduled', confirming the pod sat pending for nearly the entire eval duration
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. If the affinity is misconfigured or the node pool was recently resized/relabeled, this could compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — kata peer-pod VM quota not scaled to match eval concurrency: all three sibling evals ran in close succession (17:01, 17:04, 17:04 UTC) and each requested a VM; if the pool quota is small (e.g., 2 VMs total) concurrent eval runs can exhaust it instantly.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — a previous eval run or production workload leaked a VM allocation that was not cleaned up, reducing available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots below the expected baseline. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (source-context line 1916) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have left a dangling allocation.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if VM capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling bottleneck
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same kata.peerpods.io/vm message, the root cause is confirmed as a shared pool-level resource constraint.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and check Allocatable vs. Requests to determine how many VM slots are consumed.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: List all pods in the remote-agents namespace that are in Running or Pending state to identify any that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — kata peer-pod VM scheduling pool (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports 0/6 nodes schedulable due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that carry this resource, blocking all remote agent pod creation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which requires a kata peer-pod VM. The pod never schedules, so no evidence is collected and the contract fails entirely (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state eval checks (sibling failures)
affectedAreas.reason: Both required sibling checks (features.json line 183-184) failed with the identical scheduling error before remote-agent-runtime ran, indicating the VM pool was already exhausted at the start of the eval sequence (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — degraded/outage threshold
affectedAreas.reason: The two required checks failing satisfies the outageAfterFailures=2 condition defined in the feature registry (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).
affectedAreas.details: degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2 (features.json lines 187-188). With both required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failing, the feature is at or past the outage threshold by registry definition.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the 2 kata-capable nodes in the production-api cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs. consumed capacity and identify which pods hold the slots.
Check for leaked peer-pod VM allocations from prior eval runs or production workloads that were not cleaned up; delete any stuck or orphaned pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

If the VM pool is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata peer-pod node pool needs to be scaled up (more nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource) or the VM quota per node increased.

Verify the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods to confirm the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded and that the 2 VM-capable nodes have the correct labels; correct any label drift if found.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) to confirm it handles eval timeout and error paths without leaving dangling VM allocations that could deplete the pool across successive eval runs.

Monitor the next scheduled eval run after any remediation to confirm all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return to passing status with full evidence collected.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still present. A pass with full evidence would indicate self-resolution; a repeat Unschedulable message confirms sustained capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the 2 kata-capable nodes to inspect VM slot capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly quantifies whether VM slots are exhausted and by which pods, confirming or ruling out the primary cause.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node for each node that carries the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and compare Allocatable quantity against current Requests to determine how many slots are consumed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm in the remote-agents namespace
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs left dangling VM allocations that are consuming the limited pool capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods -n <remote-agents-namespace> and filter for pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests to identify any leaked or stuck allocations from prior eval runs.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling bottleneck affects all three checks simultaneously, validating the pool-level diagnosis versus a check-specific issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for cleanup logic
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the eval runner can contribute to VM slot exhaustion under failure conditions.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Review infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs around the withCleanup call at line 1916 to verify the cleanup path handles timeout and error cases without leaking VM allocations.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe node output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and no current consumers on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful re-run of remote-agent-create immediately after this failure (with no manual intervention) would suggest the failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

Evidence that the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude the 2 VM-capable nodes would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to a misconfiguration.
A passing run of remote-agent-runtime with full evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) collected would confirm the issue has self-resolved, ruling out a persistent capacity problem.
Logs showing the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) successfully deleted all prior eval VMs would reduce the likelihood of a leaked-allocation cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs. used capacity on the eligible nodes and warns before the pool reaches 100% utilization, providing earlier signal before agent creation fails.

Add a post-cleanup verification step to the remote-agent eval probes that confirms the VM allocation was successfully released after each run, catching cleanup failures before they accumulate into pool exhaustion.
Add a node-affinity/selector health check that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod selector, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected minimum.

Consider adding a canary eval that runs a single remote-agent-create at low frequency (e.g., every 5 minutes) with a short timeout to detect VM pool exhaustion faster than the current 20-minute stale window defined in features.json line 185.
